newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.S. reiterates trade, rights issues linked.
newsitem.headline: U.S. reiterates trade, rights issues linked.

text.p: The United States reiterated on Friday that it wants to broaden discussions at the inaugural ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to include labour and human rights issues.

U.S. Assistant Secretary for East Asia and the Pacific Winston Lord said during a visit to Jakarta that he was aware of concerns in Asia and elsewhere that the WTO meeting, scheduled for Singapore in December, would be diverted from core trade issues.

Economic ministers from the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) joined counterparts from Australia and New Zealand earlier on Friday in saying issues like labour should be discussed where appropriate, such as the International Labour Organisation.

"We do think that is the central place to discuss them," Lord told reporters. "Having said that, we believe that conceptually you cannot fully separate trade and investment issues from, for example, the environment or labour issues.

"At the WTO, we are not seeking to negotiate any agreements. This is not a cover for protectionism. We only wish to have, if possible, a discussion of the relationship of labour and workers issues to trade and investment," Lord said.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
